scope_note: Research candidates only. These sources do not authorize production thresholds, user scoring, or changes to the Stage 11 evidence registry.

sources.title: Why Visual and Vocal Interview Cues Can Affect Interviewers' Judgments and Predict Job Performance
sources.study_population: Study 1: utility-company managers; Study 2: news-publishing-company managers; separate undergraduate raters coded visual cues.
sources.sample_size: Study 1 N=60 managers; Study 2 N=110 managers; visual-cue coding used 110 students, five ratings per interview.

measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; attractiveness, smiling, gaze, hand movement, and body orientation

sources.notes: Interview-context evidence, but the visual result is a five-cue composite that includes appearance and hand movement. It does not isolate head angles, shoulders, or interval statistics.

sources.title: Hire Me: Computational Inference of Hirability in Employment Interviews Based on Nonverbal Behavior
sources.study_population: Real employment interviews for a marketing position with students from two Swiss universities.
sources.country_or_cultural_context: Switzerland; approximately 90% bachelor or master students
sources.participant_expertise: Job applicants; professional interviewer; trained organizational-psychology rater

measurement_environment.camera_angle: Quasi-frontal upper-body view for each participant
measurement_environment.landmark_model: NONE; motion history images and optical-flow-derived features
measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; hirability ratings and selected nonverbal events

sources.notes: Closest camera-based interview source found. Visual motion features are optical-flow/motion-history aggregates rather than shoulder landmarks or relative Euler angles.

sources.title: Automated Analysis and Prediction of Job Interview Performance
sources.study_population: Internship-seeking undergraduate students at MIT; two mock interviews per participant.
sources.participant_expertise: Undergraduate internship applicants; nine independent judges

measurement_environment.landmark_model: Automated facial points and head-gesture/nod features
measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; nine judges rated interview attributes

sources.notes: Nod and smile are included as aggregated model features. Model weights and AUC are not behavioral boundaries and do not identify pitch degrees or p95.

sources.title: Automated Video Interview Judgment on a Large-Sized Corpus Collected Online
sources.journal_or_conference: 7th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII), 504-509
sources.study_population: United States online workers recruited through Amazon Mechanical Turk.
sources.sample_size: 260 participants; 1,891 analyzed monologue interview videos; 63 hours
sources.country_or_cultural_context: United States; uncontrolled online indoor settings
sources.participant_expertise: Online workers; five experienced assessment-company raters

measurement_environment.landmark_model: Facial-expression analysis; exact landmark model NOT_REPORTED
measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; hiring and personality ratings on seven-point scales

sources.notes: Environment is closest to a single-webcam asynchronous interview, but published visual features do not provide head-angle or shoulder metrics.

sources.title: Speaking Without Words: A Meta-Analysis of Over 70 Years of Research on the Power of Nonverbal Cues in Job Interviews
sources.study_population: Employment-interview studies spanning real and mock interviews and multiple modalities.
sources.gender_information: Varied; interviewee gender examined as a moderator
sources.country_or_cultural_context: Multiple contexts across more than 70 years
sources.participant_expertise: Job applicants and interview raters across included studies

measurement_environment.dimensionality: Predominantly observed nonverbal cues rather than standardized kinematics

sources.notes: Strongest interview-level synthesis located. 'Head movement' is a broad construct and is not yaw, pitch, roll, relative baseline, or an interval percentile.

sources.title: The Structured Employment Interview: Narrative and Quantitative Review of the Research Literature
sources.study_population: Structured employment-interview literature
sources.sample_size: NOT_REPORTED as one aggregate N; eight research topics reviewed
sources.gender_information: Subgroup differences reviewed; no single sample
sources.participant_expertise: Applicants, interviewers, and raters across reviewed studies
sources.notes: Authoritative design and validity context. It provides no operational head/shoulder boundary and is not a measurement-validation source.

sources.title: Beyond Employment Interview Validity: A Comprehensive Narrative Review of Recent Research and Trends Over Time
sources.study_population: Employment-interview research literature
sources.participant_expertise: Applicants, interviewers, and raters across reviewed studies
sources.notes: Broad review used to constrain interpretation of interview validity. No Face-Fit-compatible kinematic statistic or threshold was reported.

sources.title: Towards Automated Assessment of Public Speaking Skills Using Multimodal Cues
sources.journal_or_conference: 16th ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction, 200-203
sources.study_population: Speakers completing four public-speaking tasks; seven were experienced Toastmasters.

measurement_environment.camera_type: JVC high-definition camcorder plus Microsoft Kinect v1
measurement_environment.camera_count: One RGB camcorder plus one depth sensor
measurement_environment.camera_angle: Frontal; devices mounted on the same tripod

sources.notes: Public-speaking proxy with Kinect 3D motion, not a single 2D webcam interview. Visual results are modality composites.

sources.title: Multimodal Public Speaking Performance Assessment
sources.journal_or_conference: 17th ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction, 43-50
sources.study_population: Adults giving four public-speaking presentations in a virtual-audience laboratory study.
sources.participant_expertise: General adult participants; three Toastmasters experts rated presentations

measurement_environment.camera_type: Logitech webcam, Microsoft Kinect, head-mounted microphone
measurement_environment.camera_count: One RGB webcam plus one depth sensor
measurement_environment.dimensionality: 2D face/head features plus Kinect 3D body features
measurement_environment.landmark_model: CLNF head orientation; Kinect joints; OKAO gaze
measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; three expert ratings on ten presentation aspects

sources.notes: Useful multimodal proxy, but learned model correlation is not an isolated behavior effect or a threshold. Some eye-contact angle intervals were annotation-derived but numeric boundaries were not reported in the paper.

sources.title: Presentation Trainer: What Experts and Computers Can Tell About Your Nonverbal Communication
sources.study_population: Public-speaking domain experts interviewed about nonverbal practices and the Presentation Trainer.

measurement_environment.camera_type: Presentation Trainer research prototype; exact sensor configuration NOT_REPORTED in accessible source

sources.notes: Identifies 131 nonverbal communication practices but explicitly reports that the prototype lacked grounding in a valid assessment model. It supplies no numeric head/shoulder boundary.

sources.title: Indicators for Evaluating Public Speaking in Adults: A Scoping Review
sources.study_population: Adult public-speaking assessment studies using observation by evaluators or judges.
sources.country_or_cultural_context: English-, Portuguese-, or Spanish-language indexed studies
sources.participant_expertise: Public speakers and evaluator/judge populations across included studies

measurement_environment.camera_type: Varied; technological or non-human assessments were excluded
measurement_environment.dimensionality: Observed human-rating instruments rather than standardized kinematics
measurement_environment.motion_capture: NO in review eligibility; technological assessment studies were excluded
measurement_environment.manual_coding: YES; evaluator/judge observation was an inclusion criterion

sources.notes: JBI/PRISMA-ScR synthesis. It shows recurring posture and head-movement indicators but also substantial instrument heterogeneity and no kinematic boundary.

sources.title: Head Pose Estimation in Computer Vision: A Survey
sources.journal_or_conference: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 31(4), 607-626
sources.study_population: Computer-vision head-pose literature
sources.notes: Measurement-method survey only. It cannot support interview behavior thresholds.

sources.title: Fine-Grained Head Pose Estimation Without Keypoints
sources.study_population: AFLW2000 and BIWI head-pose benchmark datasets
sources.sample_size: Benchmark-dependent; not a Face-Fit participant sample

measurement_environment.fps: Still images for AFLW2000; dataset-dependent for BIWI
measurement_environment.motion_capture: BIWI ground truth uses depth/pose apparatus; details outside extracted table
measurement_environment.landmark_model: Hopenet, direct CNN classification and regression without keypoints

sources.notes: Benchmark MAE supports algorithm measurement discussion only, not acceptable interview behavior.

sources.title: FSA-Net: Learning Fine-Grained Structure Aggregation for Head Pose Estimation from a Single Image
sources.journal_or_conference: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, 1087-1096
sources.study_population: AFLW2000 and BIWI head-pose benchmark datasets
sources.sample_size: Benchmark-dependent; not a Face-Fit participant sample
sources.notes: Single-image measurement benchmark. Its errors must not be converted into interview thresholds.

sources.title: OpenFace 2.0: Facial Behavior Analysis Toolkit
sources.journal_or_conference: 13th IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face & Gesture Recognition, 59-66
sources.study_population: Multiple facial-behavior benchmark datasets

measurement_environment.dimensionality: 2D/3D facial landmarks, head pose, gaze, action units

sources.notes: Toolkit capability source; use independent validation for numeric accuracy. No interview behavior boundary.

sources.title: Evaluation of Various State of the Art Head Pose Estimation Algorithms for Clinical Scenarios
sources.study_population: Controlled head-movement trials compared against OptiTrack.
sources.sample_size: 24 successfully analyzed video trials; participant count NOT_REPORTED in extracted source text

measurement_environment.camera_count: NOT_REPORTED for RGB; optoelectronic reference uses multiple cameras
measurement_environment.camera_angle: Frontal camera with instructed yaw, pitch, and roll movements
measurement_environment.dimensionality: RGB algorithm estimates compared with 3D optoelectronic reference

sources.notes: Directly relevant to MediaPipe measurement limitations. The authors' 5°/10° tolerable-error levels evaluate algorithm accuracy, not candidate behavior.

sources.title: Realtime Multi-Person 2D Pose Estimation Using Part Affinity Fields
sources.journal_or_conference: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, 7291-7299
sources.study_population: COCO and MPII multi-person pose benchmark datasets

measurement_environment.webcam: Compatible but not the benchmark definition

sources.notes: Foundational 2D keypoint method source. It does not validate Face-Fit shoulder tilt, movement, or scoring semantics.

sources.title: Evaluation of 3D Markerless Motion Capture Accuracy Using OpenPose With Multiple Video Cameras
sources.journal_or_conference: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living, 2, 50
sources.study_population: Healthy adults performing walking, countermovement jumping, and ball throwing.

measurement_environment.camera_type: Five JVC GZ-RY980 video cameras plus 16-camera marker-based reference

sources.notes: Measurement-accuracy source only. Multi-camera 3D, high frame rate, whole-body tasks, and N=2 differ materially from Face-Fit.

sources.title: Examination of 2D Frontal and Sagittal Markerless Motion Capture: Implications for Markerless Applications
sources.study_population: Healthy adults performing over-ground walking.

measurement_environment.camera_type: Two machine-vision cameras plus fifteen marker-based cameras
measurement_environment.dimensionality: Each single 2D view compared with reprojected 3D marker-based data

sources.notes: Relevant warning about occlusion, view, and person tracking, but the tested outcomes are gait lower-limb angles rather than shoulder-line tilt.

sources.title: Influence of the Camera Viewing Angle on OpenPose Validity in Motion Analysis
sources.study_population: Healthy adults performing front lunges.

measurement_environment.camera_type: Four iPad Pro 11-inch 2021 RGB cameras plus 12-camera Vicon reference
measurement_environment.camera_count: 4 RGB views assessed independently; 12 reference cameras
measurement_environment.dimensionality: Single-view 2D OpenPose angles compared with 3D marker-based reference
measurement_environment.manual_coding: Marker gaps manually filled in Vicon

sources.notes: Shoulder flexion is the arm-versus-trunk angle, not left-right shoulder-line tilt. Large camera-angle-dependent errors argue against direct transfer to Face-Fit.
